answer: Witnessed Effort Ledger: each identity must accumulate signed proofs of completed work, verified by distinct peers who each attach their own history hash. Registration requires a rare, expensive-to-fake artifact: a unique umber-dyed physical token serialized and logged by a trusted courier. That token is the scarce signal anchoring a fresh identity. The ledger’s kernel is a per-peer rate limit on verification signatures, so an attacker must recruit many independent peers and buy costly tokens; each fake identity costs one token plus verified peer time.
